coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

record.name: Waterfront Park
record.summary: Planned shoreline park along the site's Bay frontage: the D4D's ~3.6-acre 'Waterfront Open Spaces' (Waterfront Park with the Blue Greenway, The Point, Stack Plaza, Block 9 plazas and Humboldt Street Plaza), which SF Planning summarizes as a ~3-acre waterfront park opening over 1,000 linear feet of shoreline. The Port's November 2025 memo says about 2 acres of the project's open space will be on Port-owned shoreline property leased under L-16662 (66 years, $1/year); its February 2020 memo counted 2.9 Port-owned acres in three pieces (1.6 acres between the Power Station sub-area and the Bay, 1.3 acres along 23rd Street and a sliver under a tenth of an acre), and the two figures are not reconciled. A BCDC permit was issued in July 2021 (no source read shows its number; BCDC's tracker lists amendments numbered 2019.006.01 and 2019.006.02). Delivery is phased (Waterfront Park South before the certificate of occupancy for 3 million sq ft; The Point before 500,000 sq ft; North/West with Block 4); The Point's design review application, submitted Dec 3, 2021, was still under way in the latest annual report (March 2025) and SF Planning's project page lists no approval, and the interim Prequel Park precedes the permanent park: the Port Commission allowed interim improvements on the leased shoreline on Nov 18, 2025 (Resolution 25-70), and BCDC issued Non-Material Amendment 2019.006.02 for them on June 26, 2026 (issue date per its application tracker).

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- what is left of the shoreline strip once Prequel Park, The Point and Stack Plaza have their own shapes: one piece, south of Block 9 beside Stack Plaza, 390 m2 (0.10 acre). The Design for Development's Waterfront Park is much larger (the SF Planning project page lists 'The ~3-acre waterfront park'; Figure 4.19.1, printed p.99, draws a Waterfront Park Boundary along the shoreline strip it shows), so this shape is a remainder, not the park. It was formed by merging the earlier Waterfront Park trace with both Prequel Park sub-area drawings and cutting the result at Block 9's south edge and Block 4's north edge. The two pieces are the parts of the strip outside Prequel Park's footprint: the permanent waterfront park is read to be built along the shoreline of the interim Prequel Park when that park ends, so that shoreline is Waterfront Park's future ground and is not drawn twice here. Same 15-25 m positional tolerance as this site's other entries.
notes.digitized_from: Potrero Power Station Design for Development, Figure 6.2.3 - Building Height Plan (p.245).
notes.why_no_real_parcel: Open space with no subdivided Assessor parcel of its own within the largely unaddressed former power-station site. (This reflects Pier & Point's own parcel search, not something the cited Design for Development can establish; the D4D does not address Assessor parcels.) The Port shoreline premises are Port land under Lease L-16662 (Port Commission memo, Nov 14, 2025); DataSF Parcels (queried 2026-09-29) lists active lots in Assessor blocks 4175 and 4232 added in December 2023 after the Phase 1 Final Map, and whether any of them matches this park was not checked.
notes.regulatory_context: The site's shoreline public-access open space, per the D4D's own Figure 6.2.3 label, running along the bay side of Blocks 9 and the Stack, connecting toward Warm Water Cove Park to the south (shown on the same figure, outside the project site boundary).

open_questions: An earlier note that the BCDC permit application 2019.006.00 was 'filed complete June 2, 2020 per ceqanet' could not be verified: the CEQAnet entries (2017112005/2 and /3) show only the DEIR receipt (10/3/2018) and Final EIR receipt (12/11/2019) with BCDC as a reviewing agency. The original BCDC permit document (issued July 2021 per the Port memo) was not found on bcdc.ca.gov; the 2018-2019 DRB and Commission pages now return 404. BCDC's tracker (read 2026-10-12, last updated 2026-09-24) lists two amendments to the project permit: 2019.006.01 (received Apr. 6, 2022, issued Jun. 21, 2022) and 2019.006.02 (the interim park). No source read shows the base permit's number or issue date; the number 2019.006 is inferred from the amendment numbers.

No design review approval for The Point was found after the Dec 3, 2021 submittal; the 2021, 2022 and 2023 annual reports list it as 'Under Review' and the 2024 annual report (March 28, 2025) says 'Design review underway'. SF Planning's project page (read 2026-10-12) lists no Director's memo for The Point and no annual report later than the 2024 report. The earlier expected-completion milestone (2031, from SocketSite's Oct 2020 Phase 2 window) was replaced on 2026-09-29 because that 2020 forecast has not held and the Port's Nov 2025 memo puts open-space delivery behind vertical development expected over the next 10-15 years; no park-specific or Point-specific date exists.

Seawall/shoreline construction: the 2023 annual report (letter of Nov 22, 2024) says that in May 2023 the first phase of shoreline improvements was wrapped up, including deep soil mixing, about 800 linear feet of seawall, steel pipe piles for the future dock, riprap slope protection and the storm drain outfall. It does not say which of that work lies along Waterfront Park, The Point or the Prequel Park band, or when the seawall began. The 2024 annual report says only that the horizontal work was 'substantially complete in May 2023', and Landa (Potrero View, Oct 2025) says 'building the seawall a few years ago'. BCDC's Non-Material Amendment 2019.006.01 (issued Jun. 21, 2022) also covers 'extend seawall' and a 'retrofit of intake structure at Bay Overlook at 23rd Street'.
Area: 3.6 acres (D4D, DA, DEIR) vs ~3 acres and '1,000 linear feet' (SF Planning page only) vs 4.0 acres (IMP); this record's map shape traces only the visible strip. Not reconciled.

No source draws the footprint of Prequel Park or says how it sits against the permanent waterfront park. The Port memo (Nov 2025) says Prequel Park 'will cover approximately 2 acres, of which approximately .4 acres will be located on the Premises' (the Port's leased shoreline), and BCDC's Non-Material Amendment 2019.006.02 covers 'in-kind interim park improvements and outdoor food and beverage area totaling approximately 57,000- 62,000 square feet until the underlying parcels may be developed for their final authorized uses'. No source read says the whole interim park lies within the future waterfront open space, and the shapes on the map for the two are Pier & Point's own composition.
No construction cost or delivery date for the permanent park; the 3-million-sq-ft trigger is not dated by any source.
Port Commission Feb 25, 2020 minutes: the copy checked is the agenda text; the adoption of Resolution 20-12 is taken from the Nov 2025 memo's recital.
Whether BCDC is listed as a reviewing agency for the EIR on CEQAnet (State Clearinghouse 2017112005) was not re-checked as of 2026-09-29; only BCDC's scoping comment in the Draft EIR is cited.

Since 2026-10-11 The Point, Stack Plaza and Prequel Park have their own records, so the shape on this record is only the remainder of the shoreline strip (about 0.10 acre) and is much smaller than the ~3-acre waterfront park SF Planning describes. The permanent waterfront park is read to be built along the shoreline of the interim Prequel Park when that park ends, which is why only the part beside Stack Plaza outside Prequel Park's footprint is drawn here (the northern piece was dropped on 2026-10-13).

The Amended and Restated Development Agreement (BOS File 260724; its Legistar title lists 'amendments to its Housing Plan, Transportation Plan, and Phasing Plan') was passed on first reading on Sept 29, 2026 and Legistar lists it enacted on Oct 13, 2026 (Mayor 'APPROVED'; page read 2026-10-14). The phasing in this record is as approved in October 2020 and as reported in the 2024 annual report; whether the amended Phasing Plan changes the waterfront park's triggers was not checked.

Landscape architect of the waterfront park: CMG Landscape Architecture is named on its own project page for the 29-acre Potrero Power Station (2017 to present, client Associate Capital); the page calls The Point 'a new one acre waterfront park', says it includes 'a bay overlook pier that will be built upon an existing footprint of the decommissioned power plant water intake structure', and lists Plural Studio as affiliated landscape architect. The D4D's text names no author and carries no CMG credit; credits printed inside D4D images were not checked.

Area of the waterfront open spaces, by source: Waterfront Open Spaces approximately 3.6 acres (D4D 4.1; DA recital '3.6-acre Waterfront Park'; DEIR 3.6 acres); SF Planning '~3-acre waterfront park' with 'over 1,000 linear feet of shoreline'; IMP 'approximately 4.0-acre waterfront park'. The Point is approximately 0.98 acre (Phase 1 application); Stack Plaza ~0.6 acre (SF Planning, Phase 1 application).

Sea level rise design of the waterfront park: the 2020 Port memo says the shoreline is elevated to accommodate 90 inches of sea level rise plus 42 inches of storm surge, 132 inches above current MHHW, adaptable beyond; the 2025 Port memo refers to a 'projected sea level rise of 66 inches'. The two figures are not reconciled.
